Alright, let me think about this year. My land is only 1.1 mu — just that strip near the village. It's small, so I don't spend a lot on inputs in total, but every yuan still counts. My husband and I do most of the field work; our kids have jobs in town so they send some money back, which helps. With off-farm income, the farm is mainly for our own grain and a little cash.

**Wheat first.** I always plant around October 10-15, after the maize comes off. I buy improved seed each year from the agricultural supply shop — costs about 8 yuan per kg and I use roughly 15 kg per mu because I broadcast a bit heavy to be safe. For fertilizer, I put down a compound fertilizer (15-15-15) as base, about 40 kg per mu before plowing, then topdress urea around 15 kg per mu at jointing in early March when I see the wheat greening up. That works out to maybe 16-17 kg of nitrogen per mu total. The extension guy once said 15 is enough, but I'd rather put a little extra than come up short — a yellow field in spring is scary. I irrigate three times: winter water in December if it's dry, jointing water in March with the topdress, and heading water in April. Maybe a fourth for grain-filling if May is hot. The well is metered so I watch the cost. I usually get around 420-450 kg per mu, depending on the weather at harvest.

**Maize right after.** The turnaround is tight — I have maybe 5-7 days between wheat combine and getting maize in the ground. I hire the combine and I hire the no-till seeder (共用 machinery, the village organizes it) because we don't have time to plow. Hybrid seed, about 2.5 kg per mu. I put compound fertilizer down with the seeder, then topdress urea once at the big trumpet stage in late July, maybe 15 kg. Total nitrogen around 14-15 kg per mu. Irrigation depends on the rain — summer is usually wet enough here, but if July is dry I'll run the well once or twice. For pests, if I see army worms or corn borer I spray, otherwise I leave it. Yield usually 450-500 kg per mu.

I don't hire field labor — at 1.1 mu the two of us manage fine, maybe 15 days of our own work across the whole year for both crops. The main hired cost is the machinery service.
